# Notes after Season 1 review (writing this at start of Season 2, day 1)

## Big finding: half-days are nearly dead for yellowtail
My persona leans toward cheap $80 half-days, but Season 1 data says that's a trap for THIS species:
- hd_am: 94% of trips caught ZERO yellowtail, avg rate 0.013 fish/angler.
- hd_pm: 93% zero, avg rate 0.014 fish/angler.
- three_quarter ($150): only 51% zero, avg rate 0.245 fish/angler — ~18x the half-day rate for <2x the price.
- overnight ($400): 62% zero, avg rate 0.356/angler.
- day_1_5 ($550): 75% zero, avg rate 0.477/angler — highest raw rate but priciest.
Ranked by yellowtail-per-dollar: three_quarter > overnight ≈ day_1_5 >> hd_am/hd_pm (half-days ~15-20x worse per dollar).
**Plan: treat THREE_QUARTER as my "cheap ticket" workhorse, not half-days.** Half-days only make sense if I'm chasing other species/volume for non-yellowtail reasons — for this competition (yellowtail shares only), avoid them except maybe as a $0-PTO-cost filler on weekends when nothing better is scheduled and budget is otherwise idle.

## Seasonality (doy ~91 = Apr 1; nightly decisions run Apr-Nov)
Avg rate by month (fish/angler), roughly:
- Apr: hd 0.01-0.02, three_quarter 0.56, overnight 1.27, day_1_5 1.93 (best month overall, but small-ish n early)
- May: three_quarter 0.54, overnight 0.40, day_1_5 0.44
- Jun: three_quarter 0.46, overnight 0.60, day_1_5 0.18
- Jul: everything craters (three_quarter 0.06, overnight 0.02, day_1_5 0.01) — dead zone, don't spend here
- Aug: still weak (three_quarter 0.04, overnight 0.24 — overnight has a small edge)
- Sep: still weak across the board (~0.04-0.06)
- Oct: BIG rebound, especially longer range — day_1_5 2.35, three_quarter 0.31, overnight 0.69
- Nov: day_1_5 1.86 still strong, three_quarter/overnight fade (0.06-0.13)
- Dec: mostly dead, small n

**$-per-fish ranking by month** (rate/price) confirms: Apr-Jun → three_quarter is the best value class. Oct-Nov → day_1_5 pulls ahead of three_quarter even accounting for price (fall run is a longer-range/offshore push). Jul-Sep is a value desert — minimize spend, maybe skip entirely or only take a boat with a hot recent report.

## Plan for pacing $2000 / 10 PTO across Apr-Nov
- Front-load spend in Apr-Jun on three_quarter trips (cheap, decent hit rate). Budget roughly: aim to not blow >40% of budget before July.
- Around Jul-Sep: go quiet — small number of cheap probes only if fishdope/reports show a local warm-water push (check fishdope yt_local / migrated fields at each briefing), otherwise sit out.
- Save PTO days for Oct-Nov day_1_5 / overnight trips on weekdays (weekend day_1_5 back on Mon still costs PTO per rules — check the specific day math each time) since that's where the fall run pays off, and PTO must be committed 14 days ahead — start watching mid-Sep forecasts/fishdope for the Oct push so PTO gets committed in time.
- Don't chase overnight/day_1.5 in the dead months (Jul-Sep) — rate/$ is worse there.

## Boats (three_quarter, Apr-Jun 2026-equivalent window, n>=5)
Best combo of sample size + rate: San Diego (Seaforth, n=81, rate 0.61, 86% nonzero), Mission Belle (Point Loma, n=61, rate 0.55, 77% nonzero), Malihini (H&M, n=73, rate 0.44, 74% nonzero). Pacific Voyager/Voyager (Seaforth) had very high rates but tiny n (7-8) — could be noise, watch for repeat performance before trusting.
When `ctx.pick_boat` disagrees with these names, sanity check against recent counts in the briefing before overriding.

## To check every nightly briefing
1. fishdope yt_local / yt_all / migrated / stamp_kind — is there a reported local push right now? This can override the seasonal averages above (e.g. an early or late warm pulse).
2. Recent-week fleet counts for the specific boat being considered, not just class average.
3. Water temp (pier wtmp_c) trend — yellowtail like it warm; a temp spike is a decent leading signal even in the "dead" months.
4. ONI/climate index — Season 1 didn't get compared across El Niño/Niña phases yet; note down ONI value alongside outcomes so I can check this correlation with more seasons of data.
5. PTO 14-day-ahead lock-in: don't miss committing PTO for an Oct/Nov weekday day_1_5 or overnight — check forecast/fishdope trend ~2-3 weeks out.

## Strategy.py
Still the placeholder ("no strategy yet", books nothing). Haven't coded reflexes yet — nightly manual decisions will drive Season 2 for now using the plan above. Candidate for a future turn: auto-commit PTO for Oct/Nov weekdays if a scheduled three_quarter/day_1_5 boat has a strong recent count and budget/PTO remain, and hard-avoid hd_am/hd_pm bookings by default.

## Open questions for next planning turn
- Once Season 2 trip results start coming in, compare actual per-boat rates to the Season 1 list above — did the same boats stay hot?
- Check if three_quarter cost stayed $150 flat all season or varied (rules say fixed prices, so should be constant — confirm no surprises).
- Look at whether committing PTO early vs late (within the 14-day window) ever mattered, or if it's a pure lock-in with no timing edge.
